title: Mix sky colours in linear colour space in compatibility
body:
Both ```PhysicalSkyMaterial``` and ```ProceduralSkyMaterial``` look different in the Compatibility renderer than they do in Forward+ because they use the same shader in both even though the renderers pass in light data in different colour spaces. Compatibility passes in directional light data in sRGB and so in order for sky shaders using light data to look the same across renderers they must convert it to the correct colour space before mixing.

||```PhysicalSkyMaterial```|```ProceduralSkyMaterial```|
|--------------|-|-|
|Forward+|![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79aed7da-3ec2-4400-9f2f-0321c1a2a80c)|![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a6e0b30-f47a-4be2-a135-3b18a2253f1d)
|Compatibility before|![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ada2e2fc-64f2-4064-83d5-7e5143694f35)|![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/518cb38b-f322-493e-bf00-a66189c1cbc3)
|Compatibility after|![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55c204f0-6a17-493d-a702-65b386ea8b67)|![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e911315f-c74e-450d-8fab-e8fe1b8d1f37)|

The sky / ground is ever so slightly a different colour in the pictures but I think that has to do with debanding / tonemapping / something else.

I included the functions ```srgb_to_linear``` and ```linear_to_srgb``` from ```drivers/gles3/shaders/tonemap_inc.glsl``` in order to do the conversions. I think it might be a good idea at some point to expose them in the shading language, considering that they may be needed if you want to make a sky shader look the same in Compatibility and Forward+. Also I left the comments of links to where they came from but I wasn't sure if I should remove those since they will be included if the user converts the material to a shader.

While the shaders have preprocessor hints inside, they are commented out because the shaders don't go through the preprocessor. They are there so that if a user was to convert a sky material to a shader, they can uncomment them and the shader will give the same results under all renderers.

Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/84441
